description: Lightweight string utility atoms that keep string contents opaque and expose only Z3-friendly i64 facts. This task deliberately avoids unimplemented string-theory operators: safe_truncate returns a validated length bound supplied by callers, and is_ascii classifies one ASCII code point rather than quantifying over an opaque Str. The generated file MUST begin with a header comment block (// ======) identifying the module as 'std/string_utils — verified string utilities'. Comments must be in Japanese to match the surrounding std style. Each atom follows the convention used in std/core.mm: `atom name(params) requires: ...; ensures: ...; body: { ... };`. Do NOT invent new operators, types, or syntax — use only conditionals, comparisons, conjunction, disjunction, and integer constants already present in std/core.mm.
implementation_notes: Do not access Str internals or call undefined len/substring methods.
safe_truncate may return max_len directly because callers provide max_len as the bound to be preserved.
is_ascii should check 0 <= code && code <= 127 and return an i64 boolean.

atoms.name: safe_truncate
atoms.description: Return a trusted truncated length bound supplied by the caller. Output is non-negative and never exceeds max_len, so callers can use it as a slice bound without further checks.

atoms.name: is_ascii
atoms.description: Return 1 if `code` is in the ASCII byte range [0, 127], otherwise 0. The boolean is encoded as i64 so the contract is provable with Z3 integer theory.
